slides.title: Gap Analysis
slides.raw:
Gap Analysis
• Systematic Evaluation
• On-going Process
slides.teach: Read the source points, then explain the slide without looking. On Security+, recognition is not enough—you should be able to apply the concept to a scenario.

course.learn: Gap analysis compares the current security state with a desired target such as a standard, policy, architecture, or maturity level. The “gap” is what must change to reach the target.
course.why: It turns broad goals into concrete improvement work and helps prioritize resources.
course.example: A company requires MFA for all privileged accounts, discovers that 30% of admin systems still use passwords only, and creates a remediation plan.
course.exam: Current state versus desired state is the strongest clue for gap analysis.

course.learn: Security monitoring and automation tools include SIEM for event correlation, SCAP for standardized security-content automation, DLP for controlling sensitive data movement, and SNMP for device monitoring and traps.
course.why: Different tools answer different questions; knowing the purpose prevents choosing a tool that cannot observe the required layer.
course.example: A network switch sends an SNMP trap for a failed interface while the SIEM correlates that event with other security logs.
course.exam: SCAP = standardized security automation/content, SIEM = log/event correlation, DLP = sensitive-data movement, SNMP trap = device-generated management alert.
